name: Rune-Inscribed Tablet
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a stone message to young Darkspear troll shamans. It sends promising mystics to Shikrik for formal spiritual instruction.

sections.title: A Summons to the Spirits
sections.body: Gornek gives a rune-carved stone to initiates who prove their mettle in the Valley of Trials. The troll shaman Ishi-yo sends it to Shikrik, the shaman trainer. For Darkspear trolls, the tablet begins a shared path with the orcs. Their old spiritual traditions join the shamanic heritage Warchief Thrall has renewed.

faq.q: What is the Rune-Inscribed Tablet used for?
faq.answer: Gornek gives the tablet to young troll shamans in the Valley of Trials. It directs them to Shikrik for formal spiritual education.
The troll shaman Ishi-yo sends the tablet. It directs the initiate to Shikrik, the orc shaman trainer just outside the Den in the Valley of Trials. Shikrik knows they are coming.
Gornek gives the tablet to newly arrived Darkspear troll shamans as their first class summons in Durotar.

angles.text: As a shaman, the tablet marks your first official step toward mastering earth, fire, water, and air. Your strength flows from ancestral spirits.
As a Darkspear troll, you answer an orc trainer's summons. It marks a growing bond and shared spiritual path between your people and their new Horde allies.
